_about: SOSpesAI condition cards v0.2. Example protocol steps, not medical advice and no doses. Three cards (renal colic, suspected sepsis, chemical eye burn) had a desk review by the health lead against public guidelines; every time to act stays a team planning value until a clinician validates it (status TO_VALIDATE). Packet sizes are engineering estimates. Drafted with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic).

cards.name: Chemical eye burn
cards.nasa_basis: NASA Integrated Medical Model, Mars transit report: the first driver of evacuation.
cards.t_crit_basis: Irrigation starts immediately and is not delayed to identify the substance (American Academy of Ophthalmology, EyeWiki). Some chemicals cause irreversible damage in as little as five minutes; 5 min stands for "now".
no_regret: Start eye irrigation now and keep going; do not wait for Earth
Note the substance and the time
Exception: if the eye may be pierced, follow the protocol for that instead

sources.title: American Academy of Ophthalmology, EyeWiki: Chemical (Alkali and Acid) Injury of the Conjunctiva and Cornea
Review of Optometry: Quickly douse chemical burns
NASA Human Research Program, Integrated Medical Model v3.0: report for a 16-month Mars transit mission (2017)

cards.name: Smoke inhalation
cards.nasa_basis: NASA Integrated Medical Model, Mars transit report: among the top drivers of loss of crew life.
cards.t_crit_basis: Airway and oxygen come first in any inhalation injury
no_regret: Move to clean air and give oxygen

cards.name: Suspected sepsis
cards.nasa_basis: NASA Integrated Medical Model, Mars transit report: the leading driver of loss of crew life.
cards.t_crit_basis: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021: with possible septic shock or a high likelihood of sepsis, antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour of recognition. It is a limit, not a waiting time.
no_regret: Repeat the vital signs every 15 min
Run the blood panel if it is available
Prepare the antibiotic the protocol names; with shock or a high likelihood of sepsis give it at once, without waiting for Earth

sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021

cards.name: Suspected stroke
cards.nasa_basis: NASA Integrated Medical Model, Mars transit report: among the top drivers of loss of crew life.
cards.t_crit_basis: Stroke care is time-critical; onboard options are limited, so the decision is about monitoring and supportive care

packet.item: Short video of face, arms, speech

cards.name: Suspected appendicitis
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of loss of crew life; most common patrol-threatening case on Vanguard submarines
cards.t_crit_basis: Decision window of hours for antibiotics-first management
no_regret: Capture ultrasound frames with the onboard guide

sources.title: NASA Human Research Program, Integrated Medical Model v3.0: report for a 16-month Mars transit mission (2017)

cards.name: Kidney stone (renal colic)
cards.nasa_basis: NASA Integrated Medical Model, Mars transit report: among the top drivers of evacuation. NASA Urinary Health brief: 43 stone events recorded in 29 crew members, none in flight in the US segment; kidney stones are the second most likely reason for an emergency medical evacuation from the space station in the model.
cards.t_crit_basis: Team planning value. No guideline gives a single deadline in minutes: NICE NG118 asks for a pain reliever first and imaging within 24 hours. Fever with a blocked kidney is an emergency.
no_regret: Note the start time, the vital signs and any sign of infection
Give the pain reliever the protocol names
Drink normally; do not force fluids
red_flags: Pain or vomiting that does not settle

sources.title: NICE guideline NG118, Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management (2019)

cards.name: Urinary retention or infection
cards.nasa_basis: NASA Integrated Medical Model, Mars transit report: urinary tract infection is among the top drivers of evacuation.
cards.t_crit_basis: Acute retention needs relief within hours

cards.name: Skin infection
cards.nasa_basis: NASA Integrated Medical Model, Mars transit report: the second driver of evacuation.
cards.t_crit_basis: Reassess within 24-48 h; faster if spreading
no_regret: Mark the border with a pen
Photograph with a scale every 12 h

cards.name: Shingles (herpes zoster)
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of evacuation; herpesvirus reactivation in 61% of ISS crew
cards.t_crit_basis: Antivirals work best when started within 72 h of rash onset

sources.title: NASA Human Research Program, Integrated Medical Model v3.0: report for a 16-month Mars transit mission (2017)

cards.name: Jugular vein thrombosis
cards.nasa_basis: Marshall-Goebel 2019: stagnant or reverse flow in the jugular vein of 6 of 11 station crew members at about flight day 50, and one occlusive clot. The clots found had caused no symptoms.
cards.t_crit_basis: Anticoagulation decision within about a day once found; found only by scheduled ultrasound
no_regret: Repeat the scan on the other side

sources.title: Marshall-Goebel et al., Assessment of jugular venous blood flow stasis and thrombosis during spaceflight, JAMA Network Open 2019

cards.name: SANS (eye and optic nerve changes)
cards.nasa_basis: HRP SANS risk: optic disc edema on OCT in 9 of 13 crew by day 150, only 1 visible on fundus exam
cards.t_crit_basis: Develops over weeks; found only by scheduled OCT or ultrasound

cards.name: Sleep loss and fatigue
cards.nasa_basis: Barger 2014: 6.09 h of sleep per night on station missions, against 8.5 h scheduled. In the Integrated Medical Model report, sleep disorder has the highest event count.
cards.t_crit_basis: Cumulative; act on a week-long trend

sources.title: Barger et al., Prevalence of sleep deficiency and use of hypnotic drugs in astronauts, Lancet Neurology 2014
